api_contracts.item: request body {sku: string (required, trimmed, non-empty), location: string (required, trimmed, non-empty; existing or new), quantity: integer >= 0 (required), tracking_code: string|null (optional; blank/omitted stored as null)}; response 200 is the filed StockRecord {sku: string, location: string, quantity: integer, tracking_code: string|null}. Same (sku, location) re-file upserts in place and returns the same 200 shape. Validation failure is 422 {detail: [{field: 'sku'|'location'|'quantity'|'tracking_code', message: string}]} naming the offending field; nothing is stored.
StockRecord {sku: string, location: string, quantity: integer, tracking_code: string|null (null = not tracked)}; 404 {detail: string} when no record exists for the (sku, location) pair.
bare JSON array of strings: every distinct stock_records.location on record, sorted ascending, not filtered by SKU; [] when none.

bare JSON array of StockRecord {sku: string, location: string, quantity: integer (> 0), tracking_code: string|null (null = not tracked)}: one entry per (sku, location) HOLDING stock (quantity > 0), ordered by location then sku; optional location filters to that one location; [] when nothing is held (incl. a location on record with only quantity-0 records).

SkuDetail {sku: string, locations: array of {location: string, quantity: integer (> 0), tracking_code: string|null (null = not tracked)} for ONLY this sku's records holding stock (quantity > 0), ordered by location; [] when the sku has no records or only quantity-0 records (still 200, never 404); par_level: null (par level is not tracked in F1, always null)}.

persistence_invariants.brief: A composite UNIQUE constraint on (sku, location) rejects a second row for the same pair at the DB level.
stock_records.sku is NOT NULL; inserting a row without a sku is rejected by the DB.
stock_records.location is NOT NULL; inserting a row without a location is rejected by the DB.
stock_records.quantity is NOT NULL; inserting a row without a quantity is rejected by the DB (tracking_code stays NULLABLE: absent = not tracked).
A CHECK (quantity >= 0) constraint rejects a negative quantity at the DB level, even when the service is bypassed.

A re-file of an existing (sku, location) is a single atomic upsert (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (sku, location) DO UPDATE): afterwards exactly one row exists carrying the new quantity/tracking_code, with no duplicate and no unique-violation surfaced.

Initial create_table: after downgrade to this migration's down_revision then upgrade head, stock_records and its columns, UNIQUE (sku, location) and CHECK (quantity >= 0) are present again (schema recreated; no row survival is claimed for the initial creation).

access_patterns.brief: SELECT DISTINCT location FROM stock_records ORDER BY location, feeding the field-location / lookup-location option source (EP3); not served by the (sku, location) unique index whose leading column is sku.

SELECT sku, location, quantity, tracking_code FROM stock_records WHERE quantity > 0 [AND location = :loc] ORDER BY location, sku (EP4); location-leading filter + sort not served by the (sku, location) unique index.

fitness_functions.clause: The stock_records migration is reversible: downgrade to its down_revision then upgrade head recreates stock_records with its columns, UNIQUE (sku, location) and CHECK (quantity >= 0).

nfrs.requirement: Stock records survive schema migrations. F1 creates stock_records (initial create_table), so its obligation is a reversible migration that recreates the schema; row-preservation applies to later ADDITIVE migrations on stock_records (declared on those stories). The 'adjustment keeps an unmodifiable timestamp and actor' clause is N/A for F1 (read-and-record only, no adjustments) and deferred to the adjustment feature (OD3).
nfrs.fitness_function: The stock_records migration is reversible: downgrade to its down_revision then upgrade head recreates stock_records with its columns, UNIQUE (sku, location) and CHECK (quantity >= 0).

fitness_functions.clause: POST /api/stock with a negative quantity returns 422 naming the 'quantity' field and stores no row.
A direct insert/update of stock_records with quantity < 0 on the paired branch is rejected by the CHECK constraint.

nfrs.requirement: Stock never goes below zero. F1 has no pick/allocation operation, so the overcommit half of R2 is N/A here and belongs to the pick feature (OD3); F1 enforces the non-negative half at both the service and the DB.
nfrs.fitness_function: POST /api/stock with a negative quantity returns 422 naming the 'quantity' field and stores no row. AND A direct insert/update of stock_records with quantity < 0 on the paired branch is rejected by the CHECK constraint.

fitness_functions.clause: Filing the same (sku, location) twice via POST /api/stock leaves exactly one stock_records row carrying the second filing's quantity and tracking_code, and both calls return 200.
A raw second INSERT of an existing (sku, location) on the paired branch is rejected by the UNIQUE constraint.

nfrs.requirement: Every (sku, location) is uniquely addressable; a collision is resolved at write time by an in-place upsert, never a duplicate or an error.
nfrs.fitness_function: Filing the same (sku, location) twice via POST /api/stock leaves exactly one stock_records row carrying the second filing's quantity and tracking_code, and both calls return 200. AND A raw second INSERT of an existing (sku, location) on the paired branch is rejected by the UNIQUE constraint.
The integration test session fixture asserts the engine dialect is postgresql and its URL is the DATABASE_URL of the paired branch, failing fast if a sqlite/in-memory or mocked session is configured.
nfrs.requirement: Integration tests run against the paired Lakebase branch (DATABASE_URL from the post-checkout hook, database databricks_postgres), never a mock, stub, SQLite or in-memory substitute.

nfrs.fitness_function: Every /api/* route responds application/json (never text/html), and a Playwright run navigating navbar -> /file -> submit keeps the same document (no full page reload).
nfrs.requirement: The UI is the React + TypeScript SPA under client/; the boundary returns JSON only and the client navigates without full-page reloads.

open_decisions.question: Are locations a separate catalog table or derived from distinct stock_records.location, and what is an 'empty location'?
open_decisions.resolution: Derived: locations = DISTINCT stock_records.location (EP3); a new location comes into existence by filing stock at it. An 'empty location' (S2 stock-empty) is a location whose records all have quantity 0, which the CHECK (quantity >= 0) permits; no separate locations table in F1.

open_decisions.question: Is a separate SKU catalog needed to decide whether a SKU is 'known', or does stock_records establish it?
open_decisions.resolution: No SKU catalog in F1: the first filing of a SKU establishes it; any non-empty trimmed sku string is accepted. A later feature introducing an unknown-SKU rule must reconcile with this.

open_decisions.question: Where do R1's unmodifiable adjustment timestamp+actor and R2's pick-overcommit rejection live (adjustment/pick ledger table)?
